sentences.text: Researchers analyzed blood samples from 2,370 people with multiple sclerosis across three Phase 3 trials to understand how B-cell levels before and after ocrelizumab treatment relate to disease outcomes.

Treatment with ocrelizumab quickly reduced the total number of B cells in people with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while those who still had detectable B cells faced a higher risk of developing new or enlarging brain lesions, and individuals with both high B-cell counts and high neurofilament light protein levels were at significantly increased risk of worsening disability.

Switching to ocrelizumab for those with high B-cell and neurofilament light levels nearly cut the risk of disability progression by four times, and the authors state that their findings regarding the link between detectable B cells and new lesions are robust based on the double-blind treatment period data.
